prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Editorial interior for a top design magazine: a Nordic master bedroom, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.05 m, level, one-point symmetric, all sharp. Hero: the bed wall as a sanctuary, dead centre: the art, the pair of glowing wall lamps, the white panelling. The cut bed foot is the foreground.

2. LIGHT. Only key: diffuse daylight from the north window on the left wall, no direct sun. Exposed for the walls: the bed wall by the left corner reads clean warm white, just under the glowing reveal; the glass one step brighter and still detailed, a pale winter garden. The bed wall falls off a gentle half stop to the right. Each piece has a lit left face and a right side about one stop darker; the bed throws a long feathered shadow to the right, short dense contact shadows under the nightstands. The ceiling a touch darker than the walls, darkest at the top right. White balance 4600 K: warm white, never pink, yellow or grey; real contrast, never milky. Practicals 2700 K, low, no shadows: the two wall lamps glow through their fabric and lay small warm pools on the nightstand tops and soft fans on the panelling.

3. MATERIALS. Walls matte mineral paint #F4F1EC; bed wall panelled to 1.25 m in painted warm-white tongue-and-groove with a slim oak cap. Floor wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Bed frame, headboard and nightstands: oiled oak #C8A27A with a soft satin sheen, one long soft window highlight along the nightstand tops and down the planks; no mirror reflection.

4. PRODUCTS, exactly these:
a. ART centred above the bed: two 50 x 50 framed prints 10 cm apart, calm black ink brush abstracts on cream inside very wide warm-white mats, thin matte black frames, matte, no glare; together about three fifths of the bed width.
b. WALL LAMPS at x 0.27 and 0.73, just above the panelling cap: a pair of flush fabric wave lamps, beige linen-look, each about half a nightstand's width, hardwired, no cable.
c. CURTAIN, cut by the left edge: the near stack of sheer natural linen-blend panels #EDE7DB, S-fold, hem on the floor, backlit, clearly overlapping the left nightstand.
d. SILL by the east jamb: one 25 cm cream fluted column vase on a turned foot, one sage branch; nothing else on the sill.
e. Right of the right nightstand, cut by the right edge: a natural seagrass belly pot cover with a tall olive tree, crown below 1.75 m.
f. LEFT NIGHTSTAND: a 24 cm handmade sand-beige wabi-sabi bottle vase, matte, two dry stems; beside it a palm-sized speckled charcoal oval dish, empty.
g. RIGHT NIGHTSTAND: two hand-sized honed travertine pedestal holders, unlit warm-white pillar candles 15 and 10 cm.
h. BED: two natural washed-linen pillows; a natural washed-linen duvet, soft creases; one warm-white boucle-look lumbar cushion centred; a mist-grey cotton-linen throw folded across the cut foot.

5. NOT IN FRAME: floor lamp, tray, carafe, glass, books, phones, clocks, rug, basket, ceiling lamp, socket, cable, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, glow halos, HDR look, grain or vignette.
